subject: Fresco Retail: stability brief + runbook handovers
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira.k@frescoretail.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: liam.turner@frescoretail.com, sre@frescoretail.com
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 08:12:00 -0400
Subject: Intermittent 500s + 3-5s p95 latency spike since 2027-07-20 22:00 UTC

Rishi —

We're seeing a recurrence of the issues we reported last quarter. Since ~22:00 UTC yesterday Fresco's production traffic is showing p95 latency up from ~420ms to 3–5s for text-generation endpoints, and a 2% spike in 500s (mainly 502/504). Traffic pattern is similar to previous incidents (bursty checkout traffic), and this is impacting real transactions.

Immediate asks: can you confirm whether this is on your side and estimate a mitigation timeline? We need an ETA for either a hotfix or a clear rollback/fallback plan.

Attached: sample trace ids (TR-7345, TR-7348) and a short HAR export.

-Samira
Head of Platform, Fresco Retail

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
To: Samira Khan <samira.k@frescoretail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 08:25:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Intermittent 500s + 3-5s p95 latency spike since 2027-07-20 22:00 UTC

Samira —

Thanks for flagging. We see correlated alerts on our side and are treating this as a P1. Karthik (Serving), Neha (Ops), and Grace (Customer Success) are looped in.

Immediate plan: 1) Triage and isolate affected model variants / regions (ETA 20–30m), 2) Apply temporary routing fallback to a lower-latency model variant where safe (ETA 45–60m), 3) Hold a short bridge at 09:15 UTC to confirm mitigation.

I'll follow up with a short RCA draft and proposed corrective actions within 6 hours.

- Rishi
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira.k@frescoretail.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 08:48:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Intermittent 500s + 3-5s p95 latency spike since 2027-07-20 22:00 UTC

Quick technical summary from serving: we've instrumented model-level traces and have two preliminary signals —

- Autoscaler behavior: a recent change (deploy 2027-07-19) adjusted the scale-up threshold to use CPU util instead of GPU SM occupancy for hybrid tasks; under Fresco's burst patterns the controller underscales and we see a delayed warm-up of GPU-backed instances.
- KV cache churn: several large checkout prompts have different prefixes causing low prefix-hit ratio and frequent KV cache re-population (evictions observed). That increases backend compute per request.
- Model variant fallback: when GPU instances are scarce the routing layer falls back to a compat CPU-quantized variant; we observed higher tail latency on that path due to an unexpected quantization path hitting a non-optimized kernel.

Immediate mitigations applied (in-flight): increased GPU minimum pool for Fresco to reduce scale-up latency; pinned routing to the primary GPU variant while we patch the fallback kernels. Neha to confirm post-fix telemetry.

Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Samira Khan <samira.k@frescoretail.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -0400
Subject: Post-incident snapshot + proposed corrective actions (draft)

Samira / team —

Thanks for your patience. Short update after the bridge and initial mitigations:

What we changed immediately (now):
- Raised Fresco's dedicated GPU minimal pool from 2 -> 6 (reduces cold-start risk during bursts).
- Pinned routing to the verified GPU-backed variant for all production routes.
- Deployed a temporary circuit-breaker to limit concurrent CPU-quantized fallbacks to <5% of requests.

Preliminary root causes (draft):
- Regression in autoscaler metric selection (CPU vs GPU); autoscaler scale-up decision did not reflect actual GPU pressure under bursty short-lived requests.
- Low prefix/KV-cache hit ratio due to increased prompt variety (checkout flow includes user-specific metadata).
- Fallback variant executed on a non-optimal kernel path in our quantization runtime, driving high p95 on that path.

Proposed corrective actions (owners + ETA):
- Autoscaler fix: revert to GPU-occupancy metric and add synthetic GPU occupancy test -> owner: Karthik -> ETA: 48h for canary, 5d for full rollout.
- KV cache improvements: increase prefix retention, add prefix-aware batching heuristics -> owner: Serving infra team (Karthik + infra eng) -> ETA: 7d.
- Quantization kernel patch: optimize fallback kernel or provide a safe fallback route that uses a verified quantized kernel -> owner: Runtime team -> ETA: 3d.
- Synthetic load tests: add a Fresco-specific scenario in our nightly run and an early-warning alert on p95 > 1s -> owner: Neha -> ETA: 2d for canary.

Attachments: draft RCA (fresco_rca_draft_v1.pdf), current Grafana window (grafana_latency_window.png). We'll circulate a cleaned exec summary for your leadership by EOD.

-Neha
Head of Ops, Redwood Inference

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
To: CTO <cto@redwood.com>, Head of Sales <sales-head@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 15:10:00 -0400
Subject: Exec brief — Fresco P1: immediate mitigation + ask for approvals

Team —

Quick executive summary and asks for visibility/approval:

Incident: Starting 2027-07-20 22:00 UTC Fresco experienced p95 latency regression (up to 5s) and ~2% 5xx increase affecting checkout flows. Impacting customer revenue.

Root causes (short): autoscaler metric regression + KV-cache churn + non-optimized quantized fallback kernel.

Actions taken: increased GPU pool, pinned routing to primary variant, circuit-breaker to limit CPU fallback.

Asks requiring exec approval:
- Approve expedited canary rollout of autoscaler metric revert (risk: brief transient scaling behavior during canary) — Approver: CTO (requested now).
- Approve a one-week elevated SRE rotation for Fresco (additional on-call and 24h SME coverage) — Approver: Head of Sales / Customer Success.
- Approve a small emergency credit (1% of monthly bill) if we miss the SLA during remediation (sales to coordinate) — Approver: Head of Sales.

I'll take on coordination with Fresco and provide daily status to affected execs. Full RCA and timeline in Drive (link in metadata).

- Rishi
Senior Account Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Samira Khan <samira.k@frescoretail.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Liam Turner <liam.turner@frescoretail.com>, sre@frescoretail.com, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 17:34:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Fresco Retail: stability brief + runbook handovers

Rishi / team —

Thanks for the quick response and the mitigations applied yesterday. We've seen p95 return to expected ranges in the 24h following your changes; checkout error rate is back to baseline. Appreciate the clear owners and timelines — the Fresco execs are happy with the proposed canary and the additional monitoring.

A couple of asks from our SREs: 1) please share the exact synthetic test scenario you'll add to nightly runs, 2) can you provide a post-change snapshot once the autoscaler canary completes?

If you can get the kernel patch into a 3-day canary as proposed that would be ideal.

-Samira
Head of Platform, Fresco Retail
